chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a man from the Kufans, from Abu Urwa, the brother of Shuayb, or from Shuayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) while he was performing cupping on a Wednesday while in prison. I said to him, 'This is a day when people say that whoever performs cupping on it will be struck by vitiligo (white patches).' He said, 'That is only feared for the one whose mother carried him during her menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reason behind the belief that cupping on Wednesday causes vitiligo according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) demystifies the folk superstition that cupping on Wednesday causes vitiligo by attributing the condition to the mother's menstruation at the time of conception, thereby linking physical traits to biological origins rather than celestial or temporal omens. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, exemplifies the Shia scholarly approach of reconciling popular beliefs with rational and scriptural evidence, emphasizing that innate characteristics are determined by conception rather than the day of the week.

en.hubeali: H 14672 – A number from our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from a man from the people of Al-Kufa, from Abu Urwa the brother of Shuayb, or from Shuayb Al-Aqarqufy who said:

I came up to Abu Al-Hassanasws the Firstasws whilst heasws was doing the cupping (Al-Hajaamat) on the day of Wednesday in the prison. So I said to himasws, ‘This is the day for which the people say that the one who gets cupping (Al-Hajaamat) done would be struck by vitiligo (white patches on the body)’. Heasws said: ‘But rather, the one who fears that is the one whose mother conceived him during her menstruation (Walud-ul-Haiz, the one would always be the enemy of Alye Mohammedasws)’.
